headline: Agent workflows are becoming operating systems, not prompt collections
executiveSummary: Claude Sonnet 5, Fable routing notes, and Claude Code releases point to model orchestration replacing single-model choice for builders.
Agent skills and scaffolds are becoming a supply chain: slash skills, SkillSpec, Caveman, agency packs, and loop-engineering posts all make workflow instructions measurable assets.
Trust and oversight are the buyer pain: Cursor privacy complaints, agent-memory APIs, code-review concerns, and browser agents reward products that prove state, permissions, and reviewability.

sections.title: Hidden Signals
sections.description: Cross-source signals that are not obvious from any single feed.
sections.emptyMessage: No hidden signals have been synthesized yet.

items.title: Agent memory needs regression tests
items.body: Signal -> Agent memory is becoming an API surface, not a prompt habit. Evidence -> AgenticSTS formalizes bounded-memory testing, Anthropic added an agent-memory beta header, and HN reviewers warn that humans cannot review code they no longer understand. Why others miss it -> the clues are split across a paper, release note, GitHub issue, and comment thread. What to do -> build regression tests because teams need to know what agents remember, retrieve, and ask before letting them run longer tasks.

evidence.note: AgenticSTS proposes a bounded-memory testbed for long-horizon LLM agents.
Anthropic SDK v0.116.0 adds an agent-memory beta header.
HN discussion warns that code cannot be meaningfully reviewed when humans lose codebase understanding.

items.title: Agent skills are becoming a dependency supply chain
items.body: Signal -> Skill packs are turning into installable dependencies. Evidence -> Claude Code now loads stacked slash skills, Caveman sells token-cutting as a skill, SkillSpec adds risk reports and contracts, and viral skill-library posts package GTM workflows. Why others miss it -> each item looks like productivity content until you map installed instructions, permissions, and cost. What to do -> audit imported skills like packages and track token, tool, and behavior changes per workflow.

evidence.note: Claude Code now loads up to five leading slash skills in one invocation.
Caveman packages token reduction as a Claude Code skill.
SkillSpec positions skills as testable contracts with risk reports.
SkillCoach shows skill-use needs explicit rubrics and evaluation beyond final accuracy.

items.title: Browser agents move privacy into runtime behavior
items.body: Signal -> Trust boundaries are shifting from SaaS policy pages into browsers and devices. Evidence -> Cursor iOS privacy complaints, Claude-in-Chrome edge cases, Anthropic model-doc changes, and home-robot launch interest all show agents entering user-controlled runtimes. Why others miss it -> launches sell capability while support threads expose policy drift. What to do -> map per-device privacy settings, revoke paths, and extension behavior because browser or embodied agents can move sensitive context outside expected controls.

evidence.note: Cursor iOS users complained that installing the app changed privacy expectations across devices.
Claude in Chrome extension behavior surfaced as a support issue in Microsoft Edge on macOS.
Weave announced Isaac 1 home robot deliveries, pushing agent expectations into physical contexts.

items.title: Agent memory regression bench
items.body: Agent teams need a memory regression bench because AgenticSTS, Anthropic's agent-memory header, and Claude Code interaction bugs show long-running agents can fail silently when state retrieval, questioning, or review context drifts.

evidence.note: AgenticSTS proposes bounded-memory testing for long-horizon LLM agents.
Anthropic SDK added an agent-memory beta header.
Claude Code AskUserQuestion timeout issue shows interaction state can fail inside long agent runs.

items.whyNow: AgenticSTS, Anthropic agent-memory headers, Claude Code question-state bugs, and HN review concerns make memory behavior a test surface this week.

items.title: Agent flow manager
